findings.issue: Part (1) unconditionally says the added reactant changes Q. This is not true for a pure solid or pure liquid excluded from Q. Part (2) appropriately adds “If the added reactant appears in Q,” but the answer should also state what happens otherwise.
findings.evidence: The CED explicitly excludes solids and pure liquids from equilibrium expressions. Adding more of an already-present pure solid, for example, does not change Q or cause an equilibrium shift. This is standard chemistry and qualifies the source worked answer’s own overgeneralization. Revise to: “At constant temperature K is unchanged. If the addition increases the concentration or partial pressure of a reactant appearing in Q, Q decreases below K and the system shifts forward; adding more of an already-present pure solid or pure liquid does not change Q.”
